caption: Estate of Richard D. Spizzirri, Deceased, John J. McAtee, Jr., Personal Representative v. Commissioner

source.document_title: Memorandum Opinion Judge Urda T.C. Memo. 2023-25 (Decision will be entered under Rule 155.)

found_facts.fact: Lifetime payments by donee and year
found_facts.snippet: He paid one of his daughters $15,000 in 2014 and one of his stepdaughters $25,700 and $21,000 in 2014 and 2015, respectively ... (5) $58,550, $34,400, and $7,350 during 2012, 2013, and 2014, respectively, to Vivien Levine.
the annual exclusion was $13,000 during 2011 and 2012 and $14,000 for 2013 through 2015.
The return showed a gross estate exceeding $81 million, a taxable estate of $30,805,768, and tax due of $10,150,307. The Estate reported on the return zero dollars in adjusted taxable gifts.

found_facts.fact: Deductions claimed (the first four disallowed by the notice)
found_facts.snippet: It deducted as claims against the estate both the $3 million in payments to Ms. Lueders's children and the $623,255 appraised value ... emergency repairs of $22,034 for the New York City apartment and $314,890 for two decks at the Aspen property ... $455,166 for five years of estimated "property maintenance" expenses

the Estate remitted an estate tax payment of $11,800,000 ... the IRS issued a refund of $1,649,693 ... determining a deficiency in estate tax of $2,251,189 as well as an addition to tax under section 6651(a)(1) of $450,238 ... increased Mr. Spizzirri's lifetime adjusted taxable gifts from zero to $193,441.
return was due on February 10, 2016 ... extending the deadline to August 12, 2016 ... On November 29, 2016 ... the Estate filed Form 706
Consistent with the parties' agreed calculations, the addition to tax shall be reduced to $120,299.

issues: Whether lifetime payments were taxable gifts (adjusted taxable gifts)
sec. 2053(a)(3)/(c)(1)(A): $1M payments to each stepchild and residence right under prenup deductible as claims
sec. 2053(a)(2): Aspen deck repairs and Easthampton maintenance
holding: IRS determinations sustained subject to concessions: payments were gifts; prenup claims not contracted for adequate and full consideration (and not marital-deduction property); repair/maintenance expenses not deductible; no reasonable cause; addition reduced to $120,299 per agreed computation; decision under Rule 155.

steps: Return check: 2015 BEA 5,430,000 (not stated in opinion; Rev. Proc. 2014-61); tentative tax(x) = 345,800 + 40% x (x - 1,000,000). tt(30,805,768) = 12,268,107; credit = tt(5,430,000) = 2,117,800; tax = 10,150,307 == return figure (exact)

sec. 6651(a)(1) check: total tax 10,150,307 + 2,251,189 = 12,401,496; less timely payment 11,800,000 = 601,496 net unpaid; extended due date Aug 12 -> filed Nov 29, 2016 = 4 months or part -> 20%; 0.20 x 601,496 = 120,299 == agreed addition
Adjusted taxable gifts from the found payments (per donee per year excess over exclusion): 2011 71,872; 2012 67,377; 2013 92,581; 2014 74,619; 2015 35,600; total 342,049
non_reconciling: Found-fact ATG 342,049 > the 193,441 determined in the notice; the court sustained the notice figure and would not look behind it (fn. 5). At least 13 different subsets of donee-years sum to exactly 193,441, so the IRS's selection cannot be identified.
40% x (disallowed deductions 4,393,311 + ATG 193,441) = 1,834,701 != deficiency 2,251,189; the gap (~1,041,220 of base) comes from adjustments not described in the opinion.

judgment: whether payments were gifts vs compensation
bona fides/adequate consideration of prenup claims
whether repairs were necessary administration expenses

caveats: The deficiency itself is not reproducible from the opinion alone; the return tax and the agreed sec. 6651 addition are.
